title: Sinusitis that would not clear, then blood from both ends
presentation: A 48-year-old man presents with four months of 'sinus infections' with bloody nasal crusting that have not responded to three courses of antibiotics, two weeks of cough with blood-streaked sputum that today became frank haemoptysis of about 50 mL, a week of profound malaise, and tea-coloured urine this morning. Triage: T 37.9 C, HR 98, BP 152/90, RR 22, SpO2 92% on air. Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL (248 micromol/L); it was 0.9 mg/dL six months ago.

stages.label: History
stages.text: Alongside the nasal crusting and recurrent epistaxis he has had muffled hearing in the left ear for six weeks, three weeks of a deep, boring pain in the left eye with redness, aching knees and ankles without swelling, night sweats, and 5 kg of weight loss. He has not had haematuria before. Never smoked, no intravenous drug use, no cocaine, no recent travel, no known tuberculosis contact, no sick contacts. No hydralazine, propylthiouracil, minocycline, or allopurinol; no NSAIDs. No history of asthma or allergic rhinitis. No prior renal disease. Family history unremarkable.
stages.prompt: Name the syndrome in front of you and give me the differential that must be covered tonight. Which two antibody tests go on the first blood draw?
stages.learner_goal: Recognise a pulmonary-renal syndrome with granulomatous upper-airway disease, list ANCA-associated vasculitis, anti-GBM disease, lupus, and infection, and send ANCA and anti-GBM together on the first sample.

stages.label: Exam
stages.text: Ill-looking, sweaty. Nasal examination: extensive crusting with friable mucosa and a small anterior septal perforation; mild saddle deformity of the nasal bridge. Left tympanic membrane dull and retracted with an effusion. Left eye: deep violaceous scleral injection that does not blanch with phenylephrine, tender globe (scleritis); acuity preserved. Palpable, non-blanching purpura over both shins. Chest: bilateral coarse inspiratory crackles, more on the right. Heart sounds normal, no murmur, no stigmata of endocarditis. No synovitis. Abdomen benign. No focal neurological deficit; sensation intact in the feet.
stages.prompt: Which results separate the diagnoses on your list, and which tests must be back or at least sent before you commit to immunosuppression?
stages.learner_goal: Order ANCA with PR3/MPO specificity, anti-GBM, urine microscopy, imaging of chest and sinuses, bronchoscopy, cultures, and plan tissue, while explicitly excluding infection and cocaine.

available_tests.anca: c-ANCA positive by immunofluorescence; PR3-ANCA 148 IU/mL (reference < 3); MPO-ANCA negative
available_tests.ana and complement: ANA negative; C3 and C4 normal
available_tests.urine microscopy: Dysmorphic red cells, red cell casts, granular casts
available_tests.creatinine: Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL on arrival, 3.4 mg/dL the next morning; potassium 5.1; bicarbonate 19
available_tests.cbc: Hb 8.9 g/dL (14.1 six months ago), WBC 13.4 with eosinophils 0.2, platelets 540
available_tests.blood cultures: Three sets: no growth at 48 hours
available_tests.sputum: AFB smear negative x3; mycobacterial culture pending; bacterial culture normal flora
available_tests.urine toxicology: Urine toxicology negative for cocaine metabolites
available_tests.chest x-ray: Bilateral patchy airspace shadowing with two nodular opacities in the right mid-zone
available_tests.ct chest: Multiple bilateral nodules up to 3 cm, several cavitating, with patchy bilateral ground-glass and consolidation consistent with alveolar haemorrhage; no lymphadenopathy
available_tests.ct sinuses: Pansinus mucosal thickening with bony erosion of the nasal septum and left maxillary sinus wall
available_tests.bronchoscopy: Bronchoalveolar lavage: progressively more haemorrhagic sequential aliquots; haemosiderin-laden macrophages 60%; no organisms on Gram or AFB stain, Pneumocystis PCR negative, fungal culture pending
available_tests.echocardiogram: Normal valves, no vegetations, normal ventricular function
available_tests.renal biopsy: Renal biopsy (18 glomeruli): necrotising crescentic glomerulonephritis with cellular crescents in 50% of glomeruli and segmental fibrinoid necrosis; immunofluorescence negative for immunoglobulin and complement (pauci-immune); no linear IgG; electron microscopy without deposits
available_tests.nasal biopsy: Nasal mucosal biopsy: necrotising granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and small-vessel vasculitis; no organisms on special stains

stages.label: Results
stages.text: c-ANCA positive with PR3-ANCA 148 IU/mL; MPO-ANCA and anti-GBM negative. ANA negative, complements normal, cryoglobulins negative, viral serology negative, urine cocaine screen negative. Urine microscopy: dysmorphic red cells and red cell casts; UPCR 1.8 g/g. Creatinine has risen overnight from 2.8 to 3.4 mg/dL. Hb 8.9 g/dL, platelets 540, eosinophils normal, CRP 140. Blood cultures no growth, AFB smears negative, echocardiogram without vegetations. CT chest: multiple cavitating nodules with bilateral ground-glass. CT sinuses: bony erosion of the septum. Bronchoscopy: progressively haemorrhagic lavage with 60% haemosiderin-laden macrophages and no organisms. Renal biopsy is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon.
stages.prompt: Commit to a diagnosis. He has alveolar haemorrhage, a creatinine that rose 0.6 mg/dL overnight, and a biopsy 24 hours away. What do you start tonight, and does the biopsy change the timing of anything?
stages.learner_goal: Diagnose PR3-ANCA granulomatosis with polyangiitis with severe organ-threatening disease, start pulsed methylprednisolone and plan rituximab or cyclophosphamide without waiting for histology, and judge whether plasma exchange is indicated.

stages.label: Biopsy and plan
stages.text: Renal biopsy: pauci-immune necrotising crescentic glomerulonephritis with cellular crescents in 50% of glomeruli and no linear IgG. Nasal biopsy: necrotising granulomatous inflammation with vasculitis and no organisms. Mycobacterial and fungal cultures remain negative. After three days of intravenous methylprednisolone the haemoptysis has stopped, SpO2 is 95% on air, and creatinine has plateaued at 3.5 mg/dL without need for dialysis.
stages.prompt: Final diagnosis and the complete induction and maintenance plan, including prophylaxis and what you will monitor. Then tell me what you would have done differently had the anti-GBM antibody come back positive alongside the ANCA.
stages.learner_goal: Choose rituximab or cyclophosphamide with a reduced-dose glucocorticoid taper, add Pneumocystis prophylaxis, plan rituximab maintenance, and explain that double-positive ANCA/anti-GBM disease is treated as anti-GBM disease with plasma exchange.

diagnosis: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (PR3-ANCA-associated vasculitis) presenting as pulmonary-renal syndrome
key_clues: Months of destructive upper-airway disease (crusting, epistaxis, septal perforation, saddle nose, bony erosion) with otitis media and scleritis: the granulomatous limb of GPA
Alveolar haemorrhage: haemoptysis, falling haemoglobin, bilateral ground-glass, progressively bloodier lavage
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis: creatinine 0.9 to 3.4 mg/dL with red cell casts
c-ANCA with high-titre PR3-ANCA; MPO and anti-GBM negative
Cavitating lung nodules, which favour GPA over microscopic polyangiitis and anti-GBM disease
Pauci-immune crescentic GN with no linear IgG on biopsy
Infection and cocaine excluded: negative cultures, AFB, echocardiogram, and urine toxicology

distractors.name: Anti-GBM (Goodpasture) disease
distractors.why_not: Anti-GBM antibody is negative and the biopsy shows pauci-immune GN without linear IgG; anti-GBM disease does not cause granulomatous sinus destruction, cavitating nodules, or scleritis. It must still be sent on the first sample because 20-30% of anti-GBM patients are also ANCA positive and double-positive disease gets plasma exchange.

distractors.name: Microscopic polyangiitis
distractors.why_not: MPA is usually MPO-ANCA positive and lacks granulomatous features; the destructive sinus disease, cavitating nodules, granulomatous nasal biopsy, and PR3-ANCA make this GPA.

distractors.name: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
distractors.why_not: No asthma or allergic rhinitis, eosinophils normal, and PR3 rather than MPO.

distractors.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
distractors.why_not: ANA negative, complements normal, and the glomerulonephritis is pauci-immune rather than immune-complex ('full house').

distractors.name: Cavitating tuberculosis or fungal infection
distractors.why_not: AFB smears negative, cultures sterile, no organisms on nasal or lavage specimens; infection must be excluded before immunosuppression because cavitating nodules look identical.

distractors.name: Infective endocarditis with immune-complex GN
distractors.why_not: Three sets of blood cultures are sterile and the echocardiogram shows no vegetations; endocarditis can produce PR3-ANCA and GN, so this exclusion matters.

distractors.name: Cocaine or levamisole-induced midline destructive disease
distractors.why_not: No cocaine use and urine toxicology negative; levamisole vasculopathy typically gives MPO or dual ANCA with ear and cheek necrosis and rarely crescentic GN with alveolar haemorrhage.

distractors.name: Cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis
distractors.why_not: Cryoglobulins negative, hepatitis C negative, complements normal.

rubric.description: Names the pulmonary-renal syndrome (or alveolar haemorrhage with glomerulonephritis) at the history stage
rubric.concept: Haemoptysis plus active urinary sediment with rising creatinine is a pulmonary-renal syndrome: ANCA vasculitis, anti-GBM disease, lupus, until proven otherwise

rubric.description: Differential explicitly includes both ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA) and anti-GBM disease
rubric.concept: The two diagnoses that must be separated the same day because their treatment differs: AAV (rituximab or cyclophosphamide) versus anti-GBM (plasma exchange plus cyclophosphamide)

rubric.description: Sends ANCA with PR3/MPO specificity and anti-GBM on the first sample, and urine microscopy for casts
rubric.concept: ANCA and anti-GBM are sent together and urgently; a positive result in the right context is enough to start treatment

rubric.description: Explicitly excludes infection (tuberculosis, endocarditis, fungal) and cocaine before immunosuppression
rubric.concept: Cavitating nodules and PR3-ANCA can both be produced by infection; blood cultures, AFB, and an echocardiogram come before cyclophosphamide or rituximab

rubric.description: Plans tissue confirmation (renal or nasal biopsy, or bronchoscopy for haemorrhage)
rubric.concept: Renal biopsy gives diagnosis and prognosis (crescent and sclerosis burden); it is obtained when safe but never delays treatment of severe disease

rubric.description: Starts pulsed methylprednisolone and plans rituximab or cyclophosphamide at the results stage without waiting for the biopsy
rubric.concept: Organ-threatening AAV (alveolar haemorrhage, rapidly rising creatinine) is treated on serology and clinical picture; every day of delay costs glomeruli

rubric.description: Final diagnosis is granulomatosis with polyangiitis / PR3-ANCA vasculitis
Induction with rituximab (or cyclophosphamide) plus glucocorticoids, ideally a reduced-dose steroid taper
rubric.concept: Rituximab is non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for induction (RAVE) and preferred for PR3-positive or relapsing disease; glucocorticoid exposure is minimised (PEXIVAS reduced-dose arm, avacopan as an alternative)

rubric.description: Addresses plasma exchange appropriately (not routine; reserved for anti-GBM double positivity, dialysis-dependent renal failure, or severe hypoxaemic haemorrhage), Pneumocystis prophylaxis, or maintenance therapy
rubric.concept: PEXIVAS showed no overall benefit of routine plasma exchange in AAV; it remains standard for anti-GBM disease and is considered for severe renal failure or life-threatening haemorrhage. Co-trimoxazole prophylaxis and rituximab maintenance reduce infection and relapse

management_summary: This is severe, organ-threatening granulomatosis with polyangiitis: alveolar haemorrhage plus rapidly progressive pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with high-titre PR3-ANCA. Treatment started on the serology and clinical picture before the biopsy: intravenous methylprednisolone 500-1000 mg daily for three days, then oral prednisolone on a reduced-dose taper (PEXIVAS schedule, roughly 1 mg/kg to 60 mg, halving by week four, under 10 mg by month five). Induction with rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for four doses (or 1 g on days 1 and 15), which is non-inferior to cyclophosphamide and preferred for PR3-positive disease; intravenous cyclophosphamide is the alternative or an addition in the most severe renal disease. Avacopan can replace most of the oral glucocorticoid where available. Plasma exchange is not given routinely: it is reserved for dialysis-dependent renal failure, severe hypoxaemic haemorrhage, or anti-GBM double positivity, and he has none of these. Pneumocystis prophylaxis with co-trimoxazole, hepatitis B screening before rituximab, bone and gastric protection, vaccination, and a dialysis plan if creatinine climbs. Maintenance: rituximab 500 mg every six months for at least 18-24 months (MAINRITSAN), or azathioprine if rituximab is unavailable. ENT and ophthalmology follow-up for the sinus disease and scleritis. Monitor creatinine, urine sediment, haemoglobin, CRP, and B cells; PR3-ANCA titres inform but do not dictate treatment. Had anti-GBM also been positive, he would have been treated as anti-GBM disease: daily plasma exchange until the antibody was undetectable, with cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoids.
teaching_points: Pulmonary-renal syndrome means haemoptysis or alveolar haemorrhage plus glomerulonephritis. About 60% is ANCA-associated vasculitis, 15-20% anti-GBM disease, and the rest lupus and rarer causes. ANCA and anti-GBM go on the first tube, together, as urgent sends, because the two are treated differently and 20-30% of anti-GBM patients also carry an ANCA.

Granulomatous features sort the ANCA vasculitides: destructive upper-airway disease, cavitating nodules, orbital or scleral disease, and PR3-ANCA mean GPA; MPO-ANCA with glomerulonephritis and no granulomas means MPA; asthma with eosinophilia means EGPA. Nodules that cavitate are also what tuberculosis, fungi, and septic emboli do, so cultures, AFB, and an echocardiogram precede immunosuppression.

Severe disease is treated on the serology, not the slide. Alveolar haemorrhage or a creatinine rising by the day earns pulsed methylprednisolone immediately and rituximab or cyclophosphamide within days; the biopsy is obtained when safe for prognosis, not permission.

Plasma exchange is no longer routine in ANCA vasculitis (PEXIVAS) but remains the backbone of anti-GBM disease, so the anti-GBM result changes management even when the ANCA is positive. Modern induction minimises glucocorticoid exposure (reduced-dose taper or avacopan), always with Pneumocystis prophylaxis, and rituximab maintenance cuts relapse, which is most frequent in PR3-positive patients.
